gold.title: Barracuda attack; Coral and the eggs are lost
gold.note: Barracuda stalks and lunges, Marlin is knocked out (C0047 groan), wakes to find Coral and all but one egg gone and grieves. The barracuda is never named in the text and the attack itself (03:26-03:40) and the discovery of the empty nest (04:17-04:41) are wordless; end is set at C0059 so the grief over the single egg is inside the range. not in text: loud musical sting / lunge at 03:26.

gold.title: CONTROL: Mr Ray arrives, Nemo joins the class
gold.note: Songs, science question, goodbye at school. Nothing frightening; Marlin is only mildly over-protective.

gold.title: Drop-off dare and Marlin berating Nemo ("I hate you")
gold.note: Kids dare each other to swim out over open water toward the boat; Marlin angrily tells Nemo off in front of his friends and Nemo says "I hate you". Mild, but it is the imitable-risk / parent-child conflict set-up. Unsure whether a parent wants this as a separate item or merged into the capture scene.

gold.title: Nemo defies Marlin, touches the boat and is taken by the diver
gold.note: Nemo deliberately swims out to the boat against a direct order while Marlin yells; a masked diver looms up behind him (jump scare), Nemo screams "Daddy, help me!" and is netted and carried off. Borderline loud_sudden_sound: C0248 "Aagghh!" is a spelled-out scream, not a bracketed caption, so not tagged. not in text: second diver's camera flash blinds Marlin (~15:10); boat engine roar.

gold.title: Marlin panics chasing the boat and begs for help
gold.note: Marlin loses the boat, breaks down ("No. Please, no", "My son!", "They took him away"). Pure parental panic/despair; no physical threat. Contiguous with the capture scene; could be merged.

gold.title: Bruce the shark appears and marches them to the "party"
gold.note: A huge grinning great white looms out of the gloom, calls them "bites" and "morsels" and escorts them through a minefield; Marlin and Dory are visibly terrified (mostly visual). The meeting that follows (C0334-C0396) is played for comedy and is NOT flagged. Severity 1 vs 2 is a judgment call.

gold.title: Bruce's blood frenzy, chase through the submarine, mines explode
gold.note: Dory gets a nosebleed, Bruce smells blood and goes feral ("I'm having fish tonight"), smashing through the sub after them while they find every exit blocked; ends with the torpedo setting off the minefield. not in text: the chain of mine explosions and bright flashes happens between C0433 (PING) and C0434; no caption marks it, so loud_sudden_sound / flashing_light_inferred are not tagged. Bruce's black-eyed face bursting through the door at C0416 is a jump scare.

gold.title: Nemo alone in the bag, then terrified in the dentist's tank
gold.note: Nemo calls for his dad, is tipped into the tank, darts around in fright (captioned cries/whimpers) and says "I want to go home". Resolves quickly once the tank fish turn out friendly. Severity 1 vs 2 uncertain for a child sensitive to separation. 25:37-26:02 is a wordless establishing stretch inside the range.

gold.title: Darla revealed as a "fish killer"; Nemo panics and gets stuck in the intake tube
gold.note: Photo of Darla holding a dead fish in a bag ("She wouldn't stop shaking the bag", "Poor Chuckles"), Nemo bolts, wedges himself in the filter tube and cries "Daddy! Help me!" until Gill coaches him out. not in text: Psycho-style string sting on the photo. Severity 1 vs 2 uncertain.

gold.title: Submarine tips off the ledge and falls into the trench
gold.note: Marlin wakes to the sub teetering; Dory wakes screaming "Sharks eat fish!" and they fall (captioned scream). About 20 seconds and mostly visual. One of the weakest inclusions; delete if the parent thinks it is padding. not in text: metal groaning/crash.

gold.title: Pitch-dark abyss: "Something's got me", the mysterious light
gold.note: Screen is fully black, the characters cannot see and are jumpy ("Something's got me!", "am I dead?"), then are drawn to a glowing lure. Played partly for laughs; it is the eerie build-up to the anglerfish.

gold.title: Anglerfish attack in the dark
gold.note: The light turns out to be the lure of a huge fanged anglerfish (jump-scare reveal at "Good feeling's gone"), which chases Marlin in darkness while Dory reads the mask; they scream (caption). The creature is never named in the subtitles at this point - only later retellings call it a "monster with huge teeth".

gold.title: Night-time initiation on Mount Wannahockaloogie / Ring of Fire
gold.note: Nemo is woken at night, led to a glowing volcano with ominous chanting and told to swim through the "Ring of Fire" (turns out to be bubbles; "Isn't there another way? He's just a boy"). Spooky staging that ends as a joke. Categories are a loose fit: the dare is imposed rather than sought, and Nemo is apprehensive rather than terrified. not in text: red flickering volcano light.

gold.title: CONTROL: Gill explains the escape plan
gold.note: Calm planning talk in the tank (jam the filter, roll out the window). Danger is only discussed hypothetically.

gold.title: Marlin tells Dory he does not want her with him; Dory cries
gold.note: Marlin tries to send Dory away ("I don't want you with me", "You mean you don't like me?", "Don't cry"). Short and gentle, reversed within two minutes. Low-end inclusion.

gold.title: Dory stung by the little jellyfish; surrounded; the bouncing race
gold.note: Dory is stung ("Ow!"), then they find themselves inside a huge jellyfish bloom ("This is bad, Dory") and race out over the tops ("So, we're cheating death now"). The race is scored as fun, so severity 1, but they are in a lethal hazard throughout - 1 vs 2 is uncertain.

gold.title: Dory trapped and stung in the jellyfish; both collapse
gold.note: Marlin realises Dory is still inside, goes back, is stung repeatedly (SIZZLING caption, scream), drags out a limp, scarred Dory ("Stay awake!") and both lose consciousness as the screen fades. Borderline loud_sudden_sound: C0827 "Aagghh!" is a spelled-out scream, not a caption, so not tagged. not in text: electric zap flashes on each sting.

gold.title: Nemo jams the filter; pebble slips and he is sucked toward the fan
gold.note: A child is sent into machinery to wedge a pebble in a spinning fan; it pops loose and he is dragged backwards toward the blades screaming "Help me!" until pulled out on a plant strand; he is left shaking and whimpering. Wordless danger stretch 50:20-50:37.

gold.title: CONTROL: Riding the EAC with the turtle kids
gold.note: Squirt shows off, fin/noggin greetings, turtle pile and kids' questions ("Mr Fish, did you die?" is a joke). Nothing should be flagged.

gold.title: CONTROL (hard): the story of Marlin's journey is retold across the ocean
gold.note: Sea creatures excitedly retell the sharks/explosions/"horrible creature with razor-sharp teeth". Danger is only remembered/narrated, which the taxonomy explicitly says is NOT a flag. Deliberately a tough false-positive probe.

gold.title: Nemo swims back into the filter on his own
gold.note: Inspired by his dad, Nemo goes back into the filter and jams the fan while the gang panic ("Not again!", "You've got your life ahead of you") and briefly cannot tell if he is alive. About 30 seconds, ends in triumph.

gold.title: The whale looms out of the murk and swallows Marlin and Dory
gold.note: A gigantic whale rises behind the two tiny fish, krill flee ("Swim away!"), and they are sucked into its mouth ("Move, Dory! Move!"). The swallow itself (~01:06:58-01:07:04) is wordless, directly after C1160. The whale's shadow is ominous from about C1119/C1138 but that stretch is played as comedy and not flagged. predator_creature is debatable because the whale turns out to be benign.

gold.title: CONTROL: the filthy tank and the dentist decides to clean it
gold.note: Gross-out comedy in the green tank; the plan works. Nothing frightening.

gold.title: Trapped inside the whale; Marlin rams the baleen and despairs
gold.note: Marlin hurls himself at the baleen yelling, then collapses with a captioned despairing groan ("I promised him I'd never let anything happen to him") while Dory plays. More sad than scary; 1 vs 2 uncertain.

gold.title: Whale roars, water drains, the drop down the throat and out the blowhole
gold.note: Captioned whale roars, the water level falls, Marlin is convinced they are being eaten ("That's eating us!"), they cling to the tongue over a dark throat, let go and are blasted out screaming. predator_creature not tagged because the whale is actually helping them, but Marlin believes otherwise - debatable.

gold.title: False "Darla!" alarm, then the dentist nets and bags Nemo
gold.note: Nemo is scooped out in a net screaming "Help me!", the gang fail to save him, he is sealed in a bag crying "I don't want to go belly-up!" and Darla arrives. not in text: door slam / Psycho strings on each "Darla!".

gold.title: Swallowed by the pelican, stranded on the dock, seagull "Mine!" chase
gold.note: A pelican scoops them up ("I didn't come this far to be breakfast"), they flop gasping on the dock, a mob of seagulls closes in and chases Nigel through the harbour with the fish in his beak. C1301-C1310 is a comic interlude inside the range. Tone is largely comic, so 1 vs 2 is uncertain; the threat from the gulls is almost entirely visual apart from "Mine!". not in text: gulls crash into a sail.

gold.title: Darla arrives; Nemo plays dead; she shakes the bag; Nemo gasps on the tray and goes down the drain
gold.note: Captioned fish screams, Nemo floats belly-up ("He's dead"), is nearly binned, Marlin sees him apparently dead, Darla shakes the bag yelling "Wake up!", chaos with captioned screams, Nemo lies gasping out of water before being flicked down the drain, and father and son are torn apart again ("Daddy?"). Frantic slapstick tone but a real threat to the child hero; I scored 2, a parent could reasonably say 3. shouting_aggression not tagged (Darla is rough rather than hostile) - debatable. not in text: Psycho strings, bag bursting.

gold.title: Marlin believes Nemo is dead and leaves Dory
gold.note: Nigel apologises, Marlin says "Nemo's gone" and swims away while Dory begs "Please don't go away... I don't want to forget". Quiet, sustained grief and abandonment. The rubric lists "deep grief" under 3; I scored 2 because the audience knows Nemo is alive. The wordless, sombre flight back (01:21:38-01:22:12) precedes C1388.

gold.title: Nemo alone calling for his dad, grabbed at by crabs; Dory lost and confused
gold.note: Nemo pops out of the pipe, a crab snaps at him ("Gotcha!"), he swims off shouting "Dad!"; Dory, abandoned, circles in distress ("I think I lost somebody, but I can't remember"). Brief and the weakest inclusion on the list; the crab grab is too slight for predator_creature.

gold.title: Fishing net: Dory and then Nemo trapped, "swim down!"
gold.note: A trawl net scoops up a screaming shoal with Dory inside (captioned scream); Nemo swims into the net against Marlin's "Nemo, no! Get out of there" and is hauled toward the surface. Turns triumphant from about C1497, so 2 vs 3 is uncertain. imitable_risk is debatable: he defies his father, but it is framed as heroic and Marlin then consents.

gold.title: Nemo lies motionless under the net; Marlin thinks he has lost him
gold.note: Nemo is found limp and unresponsive; Marlin cradles him repeating the opening scene's "Daddy's here. Daddy's got you" before Nemo coughs awake. Only ~30 seconds, but it is an apparent death of the child hero; 1 vs 2 vs 3 is a judgment call.

gold.title: CONTROL: reunion chat about sea turtles and the new first day of school
gold.note: Happy ending: sea-turtle ages, race to school, Marlin finally tells his joke. Ends before the (friendly) sharks reappear at C1540.

scenes.description: Marlin and Coral, an expectant clownfish couple, are having a sweet moment naming their unborn eggs when something suddenly threatens them. Coral is urgently told to get inside, and the scene ends with an alarming 'No!' suggesting danger is approaching.

Marlin desperately searches for his wife Coral and discovers she is gone. He finds their only child Nemo and comforts him, but Coral is never coming back—this is the traumatic opening where Nemo's mother dies and Nemo is the sole survivor of their family.

Marlin becomes very upset and angry when he learns his son is going to the Drop Off, a dangerous reef area, yelling sarcastically about frying the children. He then argues with another parent about parenting, speaking harshly. This scene shows an anxious parent's strong fear and aggression about his child's safety.

Nemo disobeys his father's safety warnings and swims toward a boat in the ocean, and his father angrily yells at him, saying "I hate you" in frustration. A young child might be upset seeing a parent and child in conflict and hearing harsh words between them.

Marlin angrily yells at his young son Nemo for disobeying and swimming toward a boat, then a group of divers suddenly attacks and captures Nemo while Marlin desperately tries to save him. This scene shows a parent losing his child and will likely upset a 5-year-old.

Nemo is taken away by a scuba diver in a boat, and his father Marlin desperately calls out for him, panicking and crying as he realizes his son is gone. This is an intense scene of a parent losing their child that may upset young viewers.

Marlin tearfully tells sharks about his missing son Nemo, and the sharks become aggressive and try to eat the fish, snapping at them and saying they want to have 'fish for dinner.' A character gets hit and asks if they're bleeding.

The sharks are in a dangerous feeding frenzy as one fish desperately tries to escape with a mask, yelling "No, no, no!" The scene shows the fish panicking and trapped with predatory sharks closing in.

Nemo calls out for his dad in distress while he's being examined by the dentist, who discusses dental procedures on him. A child may be upset hearing Nemo scared and separated from his father, and confused or worried about the unfamiliar medical setting.

Nemo arrives at the dentist's office tank and is frightened and separated from his father, calling out for his dad while the fish around him discuss a dental procedure happening in the background. Nemo is scared and confused in an unfamiliar place with strangers.

Nemo learns he's being given as a birthday present to a girl named Darla, who has a reputation for killing pet fish by shaking their bags. Nemo becomes distressed about being separated from his father and calls out for help.

Marlin and Dory wake up in a dusty shipwreck and realize a crucial clue to finding Nemo (a mask with an address) has been lost. Marlin becomes distressed and upset, expressing despair about his search for his son.

Marlin and Dory are drawn toward a glowing light in the darkness of the deep ocean. The light turns out to be an anglerfish's lure, and the massive predatory fish suddenly appears, chasing and trying to eat them.

Marlin and Dory are fleeing in panic from danger (they scream and say they can't see where they're going), and there's an urgent moment when they must duck to avoid an obstacle. A young child might find the sudden screaming and frantic action startling.
Marlin and Dory navigate a dangerous trench and encounter jellyfish that sting them. Dory touches a jellyfish and gets stung, experiencing pain, and Marlin also gets stung while trying to help.

Marlin and Dory play a dangerous game hopping on jellyfish tentacles to escape, and Dory is stung and cries out in pain. The scene is tense and includes injury sounds that could startle a young child.

Nemo is trapped in a fish tank at a dentist's office and is attempting a dangerous escape through plumbing while the dentist is briefly away. The scene shows Nemo confined and anxious about the risky plan, which may worry young viewers about his safety and separation from his father.
Nemo becomes trapped in a narrow pipe with a spinning fan while other fish try to help him escape. He panics and calls for help as the situation grows dangerous and frightening.

Marlin gets hurt and knocked unconscious after being attacked by jellyfish, leaving him limp and unresponsive until a sea turtle finds him. A young child might worry the character is dead or seriously injured.

Marlin tells young sea turtle children about his son being taken by divers and recounts an exciting (but not graphically shown) adventure involving sharks and a scary deep-sea creature with sharp teeth. A 5-year-old may be upset by the story of a child being separated from his parent and the description of a frightening monster.

Marlin learns his son Nemo was taken by divers and may be in danger heading toward the harbour; Gill feels guilty for putting Nemo in harm's way and apologizes for not reuniting him with his father. A young child may be upset by the reminder that Nemo was taken from his parent and is still separated from him.

Nigel the pelican tells Nemo an exciting but dramatized story about how his father Marlin has been fighting sharks, jellyfish, and a scary monster to find him. The vivid descriptions of dangerous encounters may startle or worry a young child, even though the story is being told fondly.

Nemo gets stuck in the tank's filter and has to be rescued by his tank-mates, who work together to pull him out before he's hurt. Later, the group prepares to escape through a dangerous ocean current they describe as a "swirling vortex of terror."

Marlin becomes very distressed and panicked after realizing he and Dory are trapped inside a whale's mouth. He expresses despair about his situation and his broken promise to protect his son, showing visible emotional anguish.

Marlin and Dory are trapped inside a whale's mouth as it roars and water drains away, and they fear they're about to be eaten. The whale makes loud roaring sounds and the characters express panic about being swallowed.

Marlin and Dory are arguing about whether Dory can speak whale, and Marlin expresses doubt that they will survive their journey. They make a loud whale call and scream as they go over a waterfall, but they emerge safely and excitedly celebrate arriving at their destination.

Nemo and the tank fish execute a desperate escape plan that goes wrong, with Nemo calling for help and nearly falling out of the tank while the dentist almost catches him. The fish are panicking about Darla's arrival, and there's intense shouting and frantic activity as they try to save Nemo from danger.

Marlin and Dory are chased by a pelican (Nigel) who initially appears threatening and tries to catch them. Though Nigel turns out to be friendly, the chase and threat of being eaten by a predator bird may startle a young child.

Marlin and Dory are being chased aggressively by a pelican named Nigel who keeps saying "Mine!" and telling them to jump into his mouth. While Nigel is actually friendly and trying to help, the intense pursuit and his threatening behavior may seem scary to a young child.

Nemo is captured by the dentist's rough 8-year-old niece, Darla, who shakes his tank and appears to harm him; he plays dead to escape, and there are screams and chaotic moments as characters try to help him get away. A young child may be scared for Nemo's safety and upset by the loud, frantic action.

Nemo is caught by Darla, the dentist's rough young niece, and the tank fish try desperately to help him escape from her grip while she screams and thrashes. Marlin hears his son calling for him but cannot reach him, and Nemo is forcibly separated from the tank and taken away by the dentist.

Nemo is flushed down a toilet drain after escaping from the dentist's tank, and Marlin hears Nemo cry out for him in distress. Marlin becomes very upset thinking his son is lost, though the other fish reassure him that drains lead to the ocean.

Marlin believes his son Nemo is dead and decides to leave Dory behind, despite Dory's emotional pleas not to be abandoned. A young child may be upset by the idea of a parent giving up on finding their child and a friend being left alone.

Nemo is chased and captured by pelicans while calling out for his father, and Dory is also caught. After being released, Nemo is distressed and searching for Marlin, while Dory has lost her memory and cannot remember what happened. This scene shows a child character in immediate danger, separated from his parent, and very frightened.

Nemo is reunited with his father Marlin, but then a menacing barracuda suddenly appears and chases them. Nemo's friend thinks Nemo was dead, and there is shouting and a scream as the fish try to escape the predator.

Marlin desperately searches for his son Nemo and finds him in danger; characters are screaming and panicking as they try to escape a life-threatening situation where Dory needs to be rescued. A young fish must perform a dangerous task to save his friend, and his father worries he'll lose his son again.
